text.p: Copper maintained a firmer tone on Monday afternoon after aggressive third Wednesday pricing earlier in the day pushed out the nearby backwardation by $100. Zinc also took a constructive step by leaping over the psychological $1,500 resistance level into new 6-3/4 year highs, while other metals ended the afternoon kerb mixed.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index rose 0.99 points to 234.51.

On the LME, the centre of attention was copper which entered the first prompt date of a two-week span of tightness with a bang as expected, traders said. Cash/threes backwardation widened dramatically to $240/$260 by the end of the kerb compared to Friday's $130/$140. Three months copper was also firmer and near the day's highs at $2,315, up $13, after easily hurdling $2,300 resistance earlier in the day.
Zinc's drama was slower in coming, but prices finally pushed above $1,500 in inter-office trading just before the afternoon kerb. The cash/threes spread was near level at the end of the kerb.

Aluminium went quiet in the afternoon after the pricing was finished, and traders said it ran into resistance at the previous support level between $1,590-$1600. It finished the kerb at $1,584, up just $2 from Friday and off from the high of $1,597.
Lead had a weak finish at a $9 lower $658. It initially surged to a high of $674.50 but was unable to maintain momentum when pricing selling emerged in the afternoon.
Nickel also finished lower at $6,880, down $85, failing to recover from a burst of cash selling in the midday session.
Tin was $40 firmer at $5,590, but alloy was quiet and softer at $1,435/440, compared to $1,450.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended lower Monday, but volumes were light, with activity tradionally slow during the seasonally weak demand period of the northern hemisphere summer. COMEX August gold ended down $1.40 at $320.80 an ounce, with the August/September spread widening back out to $3.90 an ounce from $3.60 Friday. August gold has consolidated between $325.00 and the contract lows at $314.60 in the past week, with daily momentum indicators recovering from their oversold condition, while 20-day historical volatility has steadied around 14 percent, up from six percent back in mid-June. In the bullion market midday Monday, spot gold was quoted $319.70/20, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $321.70 and the New York close Friday around $321.60/10.

NYMEX crude settled lower Monday on news Iraq and the U.N. agreed to details of Iraq's aid distribution plan, moving Iraq a step closer to resuming oil sales. August crude settled off 34 cents at $18.99 a barrel. Refined products tracked crude lower, with August heating oil ending 0.68 cent lower at 51.67 cents a gallon and August gasoline finishing off 0.91 cent at 58.35 cents. "When the Iraq news hit this morning, it came as a big surprise. People had thought there would be more delays in the deal, so the news was a real slam dunk for prices," said Warren Tashnek, president at Fimat USA Futures in Houston.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a weather-related surge in corn and soybean futures, traders said. "Weather, weather, weather that's all I can say. I don't have anything pithy to say," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN-Amro The Chicago Corp. Dry weather in parts of Australia's wheat growing area also was mentioned but most traders said the gains in wheat were tied solely to the corn and soybean rally. Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up seven at $3.29. September was up 6-1/2 at $3.36.
